text: Hello everyone and welcome to live text coverage of the Premier League clash between Newcastle United and Nottingham Forest.
St James' Park is the venue for a showdown between two teams struggling for form.
Seventh-place Newcastle have lost five of their last six matches across all competitions while Forest, who are 17th in the Premier League, are without a win in seven.
Eddie Howe makes two changes from Newcastle's defeat at Luton last weekend.
Botman makes his first Premier League start since September as he replaces the injured Jamaal Lascelles in the heart of defence, while Isak is preferred to Wilson up front.
Having missed the trip to Kenilworth Road with a hamstring problem, Joelinton is back among the Magpies' substitutes.
As for Forest, new boss Nuno Espirito Santo makes six alterations from the defeat to Bournemouth in his first match at the helm.
Three of those are in defence with Aina, Niakhate and Montiel all coming into the starting XI.
There are also recalls for Danilo, Sangare and Hudson-Odoi.
Williams, Yates, Mangala and Origi drop to the bench, while Willy Boly misses out through suspension and Harry Toffolo is also absent.
Despite their recent struggles, Newcastle will be buoyed by their form on home soil.
Indeed, the Magpies have won each of their last seven Premier League games at St James' Park.
The players are coming out onto the pitch and we are almost ready to go here.
Chris Kavanagh is our referee today.
He blows his whistle and Newcastle get the match under way kicking towards the Gallowgate end.
The hosts go straight onto the attack and force a corner, which Trippier takes short to Almiron.
They look to work the ball into the box, but Forest quickly snuff out the threat and are awarded a free-kick when Elanga is tripped by Gordon.
JUST WIDE! Forest threaten and after an initial attempt is blocked, the ball drops for Gibbs-White in the box.
The former Wolves midfielder gets a shot away, but drags it wide of the left post.
The anticipation among the crowd increases as Newcastle look to counter.
Trippier has plenty of space down the right flank and sends in a cross, but Murillo is alert and clears the danger.

The Magpies are enjoying their longest winning streak on home soil in the Premier League since a run of 11 successive victories between September 2002 and January 2003, when they were under the guidance of the late, great Bobby Robson.
A neat build-up from the hosts culminates in Miley clipping the ball towards the far post, but Montiel is there to head clear for Forest.
Of course, it was just over a year ago that Montiel was winning the World Cup with Argentina in Qatar.
The full-back slotted home the decisive penalty against France in the final.
A let-off for Danilo.
Ignoring pretty much all footballing manuals, the Forest midfielder plays the ball across his own penalty area.
It is intercepted by Almiron but, as the visitors quickly recover numbers, the hosts are unable to capitalise with Trippier eventually sending his attempted cross behind for a goal-kick.
Newcastle do not particularly like Boxing Day.
Indeed, they have suffered the most defeats in Premier League (15) and English league history (46).
The Magpies will be desperate to upset the history books today.
Forest with the opportunity to apply the pressure after Schar concedes a corner.
Can the visitors capitalise and potentially break through at St James' Park?
Sarcastic cheers ring around the stadium as Forest's corner is only cleared as far as Aina, who sends his first-time volley high into the stands from just outside the box.
End-to-end stuff at St James' Park.
After Trippier intercepts Gibbs-White's attempted throughball for Elanga, Newcastle counter with Miley leading the charge.
Gordon's subsequent cross is turned behind for a corner, and the home fans look to rally their side.
PENALTY TO NEWCASTLE? Miley threads a clever throughball into Isak, who goes down under a challenge from Aina.
The referee takes a second to quickly assess the situation before pointing to the spot.
VAR want a look, though...
PENALTY GIVEN! Following a lengthy delay, the referee initially sticks with his initial decision and Newcastle have a penalty.
Guimaraes hands the ball to Isak, who scored twice against Forest at the City Ground last season.
ISAK!!! 1-0 NEWCASTLE! Cool as you like from the Swede! The man who was fouled for the penalty to be awarded, Isak steps up and very calmly rolls the ball past the flat-footed Turner.
Forest look to respond immediately and Elanga gets the better of Burn with his pace down the right side.
The ball ricochets dangerously across the area, but Dubravka gathers.
Sangare is shown the first yellow card of the game for a rash challenge on Isak.
He will miss Forest's next game against Manchester United through suspension.
GOOD BLOCK! Miley leads Newcastle charge again with a lovely jinking run on the edge of the box.
He finds Gordon in space, but the winger's first-time shot is well-blocked by Montiel.
Gordon goes into the book after he catches Elanga late while tracking back.
Montiel waves an imaginary card in the direction of the referee following Gordon's challenge.
The full-back is subsequently shown one for his troubles.
CHANCE! Forest threaten as they send a long throw into the box from the left touchline.
Elanga helps the ball towards goal, but just the wrong side of the left post.
The Reds have lost each of their last seven away league games against Newcastle.
You must go back to a 1-0 victory under Brian Clough in October 1988 for their last such success.
Why didn't he square it?! The pacy Elanga gets in behind the Newcastle defence.
Wood is available for the square ball across the six-yard box, but the winger goes himself and Dubravka holds his shot.
His team-mate, who was certainly in the better position, is far from impressed and boots the post in disgust.
Isak demonstrates wonderful pace to get away from Aina down the right.
His attempt at a dinked cross is looping dangerously towards goal, and Turner is forced to tip it over.
Newcastle threaten from a corner and try to scramble the ball towards goal.
But a series of blocks from the stubborn Forest defence eventually snuff out the danger.
Forest are winless in all 24 away games in which they have conceded since returning to the Premier League.
Can they buck the trend here?
Guimaraes goes to ground under a challenge from Danilo in the box.
However, contact was certainly minimal and the referee is not interested in pointing to the spot.
Forest look for the equaliser and Gibbs-White manages to get a shot away from inside the area.
But Dubravka is equal to it.
Almiron embarks on a strong run into the heart of the Forest defence.
The Paraguay international gets his shot away, but it is not the best and goes high into the stands.
We are going to play an additional three minutes at the end of this first half.
WOOD!!! 1-1! Forest are level! And it is a devastating counter by the visitors.
Gibbs-White leads the charge before feeding Elanga.
This time, the latter shows wonderful presence of mind to square the ball across the six-yard box, where an unmarked Wood can tap into the empty net.
Elanga did brilliantly under pressure to put the ball on a plate for Wood to equalise.
There was no celebration from Wood, who finds the net against one of his former clubs.
Indeed, the striker was Howe's second signing at Newcastle and spent a year at St James' Park, before making the switch to the City Ground.
GOOD SAVE! Newcastle look to regain the lead before the break.
Almiron's cross is met by Isak, but Turner produces a brilliant reflex save to keep out his header.
Forest swiftly counter and Hudson-Odoi cuts inside from the left before shooting, but his tame effort is easily gathered by Dubravka.
HALF-TIME: NEWCASTLE UNITED 1-1 NOTTINGHAM FOREST
Honours are even following an exciting first half at St James' Park.
Newcastle took the lead in the 23rd minute when Isak stroked home from the penalty spot after he was fouled by Aina in the box.
But Forest did not lie down and equalised in stoppage time through a former Magpies striker, as Wood rounded off a swift counter by slotting into the empty net.
Newcastle enjoyed 61.5 per cent of the possession during the first half.
However, Forest had more shots on target with eight to their opponents' seven.
Neutrals will be hoping for an equally entertaining second half.
The referee blows his whistle and Forest get the ball rolling again in the second half.
CHANCE! The visitors go straight onto the attack and should be in front.
Elanga's ball into the box is met by Gibbs-White, but he can only direct his header wide of the left post.
WHAT A BLOCK! Forest threaten again and Aina just about keeps the ball in play to send it across the box.
The ball ricochets kindly for Danilo, but Burn is there to make an important block for Newcastle.
CHANCE! The visitors have another opportunity as Gibbs-White does well in the box to feed the ball into the advancing Elanga.
But the latter sends his shot straight at Dubravka.
WOOD!!! 2-1 FOREST! The visitors complete the turnaround and, once again, the former Newcastle striker comes back to haunt his old club.
Forest counter with Elanga leading the charge before finding Wood with a precise throughball.
The forward brilliantly turns Burn inside out, before lifting the ball over Dubravka with a delightful finish.
The two players who combined for Forest's first goal do so again.
Elanga set the visitors moving on the counter before brilliantly finding Wood.
Newcastle turn straight to the bench as Howe makes a double substitution.
The first of these sees Wilson introduced in place of Almiron.
Livramento also comes on at left-back for Burn, who has endured a torrid day against Elanga.
The hosts look to respond and Guimaraes embarks on a jinking run before finding Trippier.
The skipper sends in a cross from the right, but Turner punches clear.
WOOD!!! HAT-TRICK HERO! 3-1 FOREST! The visitors are in dreamland! The Newcastle defence switches off and Wood times his run brilliantly to latch onto Murillo's long ball.
The former Magpies striker then demonstrates wonderful composure to jink around Dubravka before slotting into the empty net.
Murillo looks delighted at providing the assist, with the defender's long ball completely catching Newcastle off guard and releasing Wood on goal.
The Newcastle fans have been stunned into silence by the events of the second half.
This has been brilliant from Forest.
As things stand - and most importantly for Forest - they will move five points clear of the relegation zone should this scoreline remain at St James' Park.
What a tackle! Newcastle seek a route back into the game with a swift counter.
The ball is played across towards Guimaraes, but a perfectly timed sliding challenge by Danilo denies the hosts.
End-to-end stuff again! After denying Elanga a clear sight on goal, Newcastle counter and Isak embarks on a jinking run into the heart of the Forest defence.
His eventual shot is deflected behind for a corner.
JUST WIDE! The hosts continue to ask questions of the Forest defence.
Miley gets a shot away inside the box, but drags his attempt just wide of the left post.
Forest make a double change.
The first sees Montiel make way to be replaced by Williams at right-back.
Sangare is also given a breather by the visitors.
Yates goes on in his place.
Newcastle also turn to the bench and introduce Joelinton for the final 20 minutes.
Longstaff is the player to make way.
Good save! Forest survive again as Isak is found at the far post, but Turner does well to block his shot.
Gordon is then thwarted on the line by the well-placed Niakhate.
There was a VAR check for handball against Niakhate.
The ball did appear to strike the Forest defender on the hand, but he could not do much about it from such close range.
No penalty is given.
We are into the final quarter of an hour of this pulsating game at St James' Park, where Forest have come from behind to lead 3-1.
Can the visitors see this out, or will Newcastle hit back?
Despite their commanding position in this game, Forest will still be wary.
After all, they have dropped eight points from winning positions away from home in the Premier League this season.
Newcastle make a change with Hall coming on to replace Botman at the back.
There is also activity on the Forest bench with Dominguez introduced in place of Hudson-Odoi.
Are Newcastle set for more Boxing Day misery? If this scoreline remains, it would be their record-extending 47th league defeat on December 26.
Williams prevents Isak from taking a quick throw-in for Newcastle.
The Wales international goes into the book for his troubles.
Guimaraes' frustration is evident.
The Brazilian kicks out at Yates, who had stripped him of the ball, and is yellow-carded.
Forest have the ball and they neatly maintain possession as the clock ticks down at St James' Park.
Given their struggles on the road since returning to the Premier League, this is a hugely welcome upturn in fortunes.
Dragging back Gibbs-White as the Forest midfielder looked to latch onto a loose ball, Schar is shown a yellow card for doing so.
The lively Elanga, who has set up two of Wood's three goals, is given a well-earned rest.
He is replaced by Worrall.
Danilo is also given a breather with Kouyate replacing him for the dying moments.
We are into the second of six additional minutes at the end of this game.
Can Newcastle launch a late rally?
Following a decent spell of pressure, Isak gets a shot away for Newcastle, but it is straight at Turner.
The hosts continue to threaten, but their momentum stalls as an overhit cross goes behind for a goal-kick.
Good defending by Worrall.
Newcastle continue to press in search of a second goal.
A diagonal ball into the box is volleyed across the six-yard area by Livramento looking for Wilson.
But Worrall reacts well to get to the ball first and head it to safety.
FULL-TIME: NEWCASTLE UNITED 1-3 NOTTINGHAM FOREST
Nuno Espirito Santo earns his first victory in charge of Nottingham Forest, while snapping their seven-game winless streak in emphatic fashion at St James' Park.

Former Newcastle United striker Chris Wood came back to haunt his old side, cancelling out Alexander Isak's first-half penalty with a sublime hat-trick to move the Reds five points clear of the Premier League's relegation zone.
As for Newcastle, that is now six defeats in seven matches and boos rung around the stadium on the final whistle.
Forest will look to build on their momentum when they host Manchester United on December 30, while the Magpies seek a response when they travel to Liverpool two days later.
That's all for today.
Until next time, goodbye!
